Definition: a primary preposition and adverb; properly, up; but (by extension) used (distributively) severally, or (locally) at (etc.):--and, apiece, by, each, every (man), in, through. In compounds (as a prefix) it often means (by implication) repetition, intensity, reversal, etc.
BiblicalUsage: The word means up, and by extension it means each, or apiece: the labourers hired at the eleventh hour received every man a penny, and the four beasts had each of them six wings. It is a small word that does the work of counting — each one, every man, apiece — and it also carries the sense of 'up' in the compounds built on it.
TheologicalSignificance: A preposition carries no theology of its own; its weight is in the counting — every man a penny, each beast six wings — and in the upward direction of the words built on it.
